newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 21.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
KESRI TOO DEMANDS LALOO'S RESIGNATION

Sitaram Kesri, Congress party president, has demanded the resignation of Bihar Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav. Kesri asked Laloo to step down during an interview to a private television channel. Until now Kesri had avoided issuing any statement on Laloo Yadav's refusal to quit office after being indicted in a corruption case.
The Economic Times
GOVERNMENT TO ROLL OVER UNEXPECTED EXPENDITURE

The Finance Ministry will not compromise on its fiscal deficit target of 4.5 percent of the gross domestic product and therefore will pass certain unforeseen expenditure on to the next fiscal. Ministry sources said the additional finance burden caused by implementing the fifth pay commission report may be met only in fiscal 1998/99 (April-March). The centre may have to shell out an extra 50 billion rupees because it will have to transfer 29 percent of all central revenues to the states under a new formula. Since this needs a constitutional amendment the actual implementation will take place only in fiscal 1998/99.
BOURSE REGULATOR TURNS DOWN HOECHST'S PLEA

The bourse regulator, Security and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), rejected German pharma company Hoechst's application seeking exemption from a 20 percent public issue to raise its stake in its Indian affiliate. The SEBI also put on hold a similar request from the Swiss food giant Nestle. It rejected Hoechst's application saying it was a secondary market transaction. Hoechst has decided to increase its stake in the Indian pharmaceutical company Hoechst Marion Roussel (HMRL) from 50.1 to 56.1 percent.
ESSAR TELECOM TO RAISE $100MLN FROM OVERSEAS MARKET

The Essar Telecom is finalising plans to raise $100 million in the overseas market for financing its cellular service project in Punjab. It is considering three options namely the floating rate note, the fixed rate bonds and the foreign bank loans. The company is awaiting finance ministry approval to raise funds. The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation said in its report the project requires an investment of $180 million. Out of this $80 million will be raised through equity participation. The remaining $100 million will be raised through external commercial borrowings.
Financial Express
ASSET-LIABILITY MISMATCH FOR BANKS LIKELY

The liquidity overhang has forced commercial banks to swoop on long term government securities in a big way. This may trigger an asset-liability mismatch for a few of the banks. The sudden shift in focus also signals that banks are expecting long term interest rates to dip further. Last week the 30-billion-rupee six year auction drew around 130 billion rupee worth of bids. Treasury chiefs are expecting another round of government borrowing to absorb the excess liquidity. Market observers feel the Reserve Bank is consciously keeping away from absorbing the liquidity.
FALL IN STATE BANK OF INDIA'S CREDIT OFFTAKE

The State Bank of India's (SBI's) credit offtake fell by about 20 billion rupees in the first quarter of fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) despite a cut in its prime lending rate. The cut in prime lending rate failed to stimulate the non-food credit offtake in the SBI. The banking industry in total recorded a negative growth of 42.53 billion rupees in non-food credit in the first quarter of 1997/98. The SBI's market share in all non-food credit is pegged at 22.2 percent.
Business Standard
INFLATION DIPS TO 4.7 PCT

The annual rate of inflation fell to a 52 week low of 4.7 percent for the week ended July 5. It was 5.9 percent a week earlier. The decline was due to the wearing off of the direct effect of the petroleum price hike last July. The official wholesale price index for all commodities (base 1981/82= 1000 rose by 0.2 to touch 325 (provisional) percent during the week against 324.5 a week earlier.
GOVERNMENT TO BEGIN FULL FLOAT EXERCISES

The government will start implementing capital account convertibility by introducing the foreign exchange management act (FEMA) bill in parliament this week. The FEMA is expected to empower the dealers authorised by the Reserve Bank to approve and manage the foreign exchange requirements of resident Indians. The Reserve Bank will supervise and regulate the authorised dealers and evolve policies for foreign exchange management.
The Observer
INDUSTRIES TO SEEK BIG CHANGE IN INFRASTRUCTURE POLICY

Industrialists may seek radical changes in infrastructure policies at their meeting with Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Tuesday. Representatives of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, The Confederation of Indian Industries and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry will demand fine-tuning of policies in the power sector, more incentives under the build-operate-transfer and build-operate-own schemes and a hydrocarbon policy. They may also seek a fuel linkage policy, extension of counter-guarantees in power projects and more incentives to explore new oil wells.
BOURSE REGULATOR TO BAN FUND-BASED DEALS

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has decided to ban all fund-based activities of merchant bankers to make them more competent and transparent. SEBI discussed the issue with the Association of Merchant Bankers on July 14 at a meeting in Bombay and sent a detailed report to the Finance Ministry. SEBI is also considering proposals to slash the number of merchant bankers, especially of those in the first category. It will also conduct a detailed inquiry into the administrative set up of the merchant bankers. The bourse regulator proposes to raise the limit of net worth of merchant bankers from 50 million rupees to 150 million rupees.
